provisional_claims.summary: Campaign defects: (1) runtime.execution_version ignored the recorded release (always conservation-2) — now uses definition runtime id; (2) publish accepted stale workers via `generation = ? OR owner != ?` — now requires matching generation AND owner; (3) publish committed branch state before inserting checkpoint/report (non-atomic; crash loses checkpoint) — now one transaction; (4) compact ignored protected lineage checkpoints of descendants; (5) fork re-applied care already performed at the checkpoint offset (used <=, now <).
provisional_claims.reproduction: create classic-1 campaign with rain_barrel treatment: results matched conservation-2 semantics. Claim, let lease expire, reclaim by worker B, then worker A publishes -> previously accepted. Fork child at offset k then compact parent with every=5 -> child's lineage checkpoint deleted and provenance fails. Fork at offset where treatment has event -> event executed twice.

provisional_claims.summary: History defects: (1) replay checkpoint cache key used only the last event (events[-1:]) so different histories sharing a final event reused wrong cached state; (2) resolved references used authoring-time local ID bindings instead of the referenced entity's current local ID, so corrections that renumber objects redirected edits to unrelated objects; (3) correct() canonicalised numeric IDs in replacements against the head garden rather than the garden at that point in history; (4) cherry-pick identified shared actions by command digest, merging independently authored identical actions — now uses event identity; (5) rebase order check ignored the local branch's authored order; (6) rebase used the parent's current head as merge base instead of the recorded fork base_revision.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create history; append note A, note B, edit_note ident 2; correct removing A -> previously edit targeted wrong/missing note (B renumbered to 1); now edits B. Fork, advance parent, rebase fork -> previously base = parent's new head, so parent's new events appeared as local deletions/conflicts. Cherry-pick an identical 'water' command authored independently -> previously dropped.

provisional_claims.summary: Workspace catalog upgrade of format-1 databases rebuilt the label index with the old (casefold-only) key function before installing the NFKC/whitespace-normalizing key, so the index disagreed with search queries; now installs the new key first then REINDEXes. Field calibration estimate used uncentered sums (catastrophic cancellation for large/fractional epoch timestamps) and weighted duplicate timestamps individually; now averages readings sharing a timestamp and fits a centered least-squares line.
provisional_claims.reproduction: estimate() with timestamps near 1.7e9+0.25 returned a wildly wrong slope vs same readings at 0/60/120 (now both 43.5). Opening a v1 catalog containing 'Ｆield  Pond' then search('field pond') via index returned inconsistent results.

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation: (1) irrigation_flow.allocate skipped residual (reverse) arcs during augmentation, so it was a greedy path search rather than a maximum flow and could under-deliver when an early path blocked a better routing; reverse arcs are now traversable. (2) irrigation.solve deduplicated search states by aggregate census + tank level, merging distinct gardens with equal averages and discarding futures that differ later; states are now identified by their full world save, offset and remaining water.
provisional_claims.reproduction: allocate([s->a 1, a->b 1, s->b 1, a->x 1, b->y 1], 's', {'x':1,'y':1}, 5): DFS first sends s->a->b->y then cannot reach x without cancelling a->b; old code delivered 1, fixed delivers 2. solve() on a garden where watering tile A vs tile B yields identical census but different later vitality returned a suboptimal schedule.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble defects: (1) summarize paired all complete controls positionally with treatment rows (zip of controls.values()) so deltas mixed different gardens when a replicate was excluded — now pairs by replicate label; (2) cache hits adopted the cached origin's identity, so two sources with equal saves collapsed into one replicate label — identity is always the requested replicate/treatment; (3) report() recomputed the result from current node outcomes, so published reports for earlier revisions changed after edits — now returns the archived envelope; (4) publish validated only previously-known reads, so a trial computed from superseded inputs (edit between prepare and publish on a never-computed node) was accepted — now validates the reads actually used by the computation.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create ensemble with two identical source saves -> report listed one replicate twice. Edit a plan after revision 0 report, finish work, then report --revision 0 -> result differed from archive. prepare ticket, edit source, publish -> accepted stale result.

provisional_claims.summary: Study defects: (1) stage decision was taken as soon as any one source had all trials complete (readiness.common non-empty), so worker completion order decided promotion and a stage with no eligible garden never recorded its failed decision — now waits for all stage trials to be terminal; (2) later stages started every treatment from the previous stage's control checkpoint, discarding earlier care — now continues each treatment from its own checkpoint.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create examples/study.json; work with --offsets large so north finishes first: stage 0 report was written with south jobs still pending (south excluded). Stage 1 treatment world state equals control's world at stage 0 end (treatment's care lost). If all controls fail, study stays 'running' forever with no report.

provisional_claims.summary: Field courier CRDT fixes: event contexts are now per-record clocks (record_clock) instead of the whole packet clock, so merging a projected selection no longer makes later edits of other observations supersede concurrent edits the recipient never saw; checkpoint records each record's own coverage (record_clock) rather than the global clock (a checkpoint after merging a projection no longer claims to cover unseen events); merged packet counter advances past any of the left writer's events seen in the right packet (prevents dot reuse when merging an older copy of a writer). Also (overlapping with concurrent edits): precedes compares the left clock's peers, _covered uses the record's own context, conflicting dot reuse compares whole events, edit-vs-delete stays visible, exact-case values preserved, project keeps only selected contexts, acknowledged uses the minimum over named peers.
provisional_claims.reproduction: desk writes r1,r2; field merges; desk edits r2 then r1; field merges project(desk,['r1']) then edits r2; merge(field, desk) previously showed only field's r2 text (desk's concurrent edit silently lost); now r2 is conflicted with both values. merge(old_desk_copy, new_desk) then put() reused an existing dot and later merges raised 'writer sequence reused'.

provisional_claims.summary: history_exchange reconciliation: (1) _common_bases truncated maximal common ancestors to one (maximal[:1]), so criss-cross histories merged against an arbitrary single base and the virtual-base merge in comparison() was dead code; now all maximal bases are merged. (2) reconcile(left,right) produced different event orders depending on argument order, so two collaborators who both combined the same pair later hit 'order-conflict'; the top-level merge now orders the two publications canonically (sorted, same convention comparison() uses), making reconcile symmetric.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two installations A,B share a channel; each adds a note and publishes (pA,pB); A.reconcile(pA,pB) and B.reconcile(pB,pA); each then edits/adds notes on its merged checkout, publishes, exchanges parcels and reconciles again -> previously HistoryConflict order-conflict; now 'merged' with a1 revised, b1 revised, b2, base on both sides with identical worlds.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge._logical_id ignored the replica origin and mapped every record to ["base", id], so records independently created on both replicas with the same local number were merged (or conflicted) as if they were one inherited record. Now inherited ids keep ["base", id] while new ids are namespaced by origin, so both survive with fresh unique local ids recorded in the receipt allocation.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Base save with next_id=1; left adds note 'desk' (id 1), right adds note 'field' (id 1); reconcile(base,left,right,left_origin='desk',right_origin='field') previously returned a conflict on /records/notes/["base",1]/text; now returns ready with two notes ids 1 and 2.

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation & ecology: (1) state.validate reset the identifier set per collection so the same ID could appear in two collections (IDs come from one global counter); (2) history days had to strictly increase but equal days were accepted; (3) Hush comfort penalty applied to glowcaps although docs say glowcaps remain suited to Hush; (4) World.index accepted booleans as coordinates (isinstance) — now strict integers like other validators.

provisional_claims.summary: courier CRDT fixes: precedes() iterated the second clock's peers so events unseen by another writer were treated as superseded; _covered() used the max context over all records instead of the event's own record (projections/other notes dropped unrelated events); merge only compared 'record' when detecting reused event identities; observations() case-folded values, collapsing distinct concurrent spellings; a concurrent edit+delete hid the observation (any False instead of all False); project() kept contexts of unselected records, so merging a selection into a full notebook dropped its other observations; acknowledged() used max instead of min across peers; put() aliased caller-owned values; merged packet counter could reuse the left writer's already-used sequence numbers.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two packets edit n1 concurrently to 'Fern unfurled' / 'fern unfurled' -> previously one value shown; remove(c,'n2') concurrent with put(d,'n2',...) -> n2 disappeared; merge(full, project(checkpoint(full),['n1'])) dropped n2; acknowledged({'desk':{'desk':5},'field':{'desk':3}},['desk','field']) returned 5 instead of 3.

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation load_design accepted saved reports whose retained tank water ('remaining') no longer matched the replayed schedule; it now verifies remaining along with world, score and trace.

provisional_claims.summary: Ecology nutrient accounting: (1) the daily +1 nutrient recovery was applied to every tile before the plant branch, so plants at 1 nutrient no longer received the hunger penalty (cell.nutrients < upkeep); recovery now applies only to bare ground as documented. (2) The 'severe strain' nutrient return checked the previous day's vitality instead of the plant's vitality after the day's growth. Verified by exactly reproducing examples/first-garden.json (seed 34, 16x11, 24 days: cells, journal and weather) and examples/lantern-hollow.json (seed 34 + examples/hollow-actions.json), both previously 17 differing cells / mismatched journal.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34,16,11); step(w,24); compare w.to_dict()['cells'] and ['journal'] with examples/first-garden.json -> previously 17 cells differed (e.g. moss vitality 100 vs 93, clover nutrients 33 vs 35) and day-21 journal said 9 glowcaps instead of 8; now identical.

provisional_claims.summary: Bare-ground nutrient recovery (+1/day) was applied to planted cells before the upkeep check, so a plant on 1 nutrient avoided the 'hungry soil' comfort penalty (and journal diverged). Recovery now applies only to bare ground, as documented.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); step 24 days; compare with examples/first-garden.json: 17 cells differed (vitality +7 on nutrient-starved plants) and journal differed; after fix cells and journal match exactly.

provisional_claims.summary: Three fixes: (1) workspace_catalog: an existing catalog database without a catalog_format row was treated as current format, so its label index built with the old casefold-only key was never rebuilt and searches with spacing/fullwidth normalization missed receipts; unversioned catalogs that already hold receipts are now treated as format 1 and upgraded (REINDEX). (2) gardening.harvest only subtracted 5 from age, so a plant well past harvest age could be harvested again immediately; harvesting now starts a new growth period (age 0, as collect_seed does). (3) analysis.transect used 'e2 > dy' instead of canonical Bresenham 'e2 >= dy', producing a different tile path on tie steps (e.g. (0,0)->(1,2) gave (0,1) instead of (1,1)).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a sqlite catalog with receipts and an index on catalog_key(label) (casefold) but no catalog_format row; open WorkspaceCatalog and search 'field pond' for label 'Field  Pond' -> previously 0 results. Harvest a moss aged 20 twice in a row -> previously both succeeded. transect(w,0,0,1,2) -> previously [(0,0),(0,1),(1,2)].

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation accepted journals of up to 200 entries although the documented save contract (README, GROWING) and the engine retain only the last 100 journal events; World.from_dict now rejects journals longer than 100 entries as inconsistent data.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d = create(1,4,4).to_dict(); d['journal'] = [{'day':0,'text':'x'}]*150; World.from_dict(d) was accepted; now raises ValueError('Invalid journal'). lantern-hollow replay oracle and smoke tests still pass.

provisional_claims.summary: Nursery: hydrated days improved vigor only for 'growing' batches; docs say hydrated days improve a batch's vigor (ready batches still need and benefit from watering) — now +3 for any hydrated living batch. Patch survey: patches were listed smallest-first; now largest connected patch first (ties by first tile).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Start a clover batch (ready after 2 days), keep watering: vitality stuck at 66 after ready; now keeps rising to 100. analysis.patches on a garden with a 1-tile and a 5-tile patch returned the 1-tile patch first.

provisional_claims.summary: Studies: an unsupported historical execution (recorded runtime fingerprint no longer matching the installation) was not detected before claiming work; advance() raised inside compute and work_once recorded it as an ordinary trial failure, permanently failing jobs and potentially committing a failed stage decision. StudyStore.claim now verifies the recorded runtime inside its transaction (like CampaignStore.claim), so the call fails clearly and leaves all jobs untouched and resumable after restoring the installation. Also hardened field_calibration.estimate to reject non-numeric/boolean timestamps, moisture and target times and rows missing required keys with ValueError instead of coercing strings or raising KeyError.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a study from examples/study.json, change the stored definition's runtime fingerprint (simulating an installation change), call work_once -> previously the job became 'failed' with 'historical simulation kernel has changed'; now ValueError is raised and all jobs remain 'ready'. estimate([{'timestamp':'0','moisture':4}],1) previously returned 4.0.

provisional_claims.summary: CampaignStore.work_once caught every Exception from compute and recorded it as a failed branch. Only intervention failures (ValueError from commands/growth) should be recorded; environment/installation errors (e.g. OSError reading kernel files while resolving the release, programming errors) were permanently marking branches 'failed' so the campaign could never complete even after the problem was fixed. It now records only ValueError failures; other errors propagate without changing durable progress, leaving the branch reclaimable after its lease.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Patch runtime.version_info (or make a kernel file unreadable) so execute_for raises OSError during CampaignStore.work_once -> previously branch status became 'failed' with the OSError text; now the OSError propagates and the branch stays 'running' until lease expiry, then is reclaimed and completes normally.
